messages:
lucy: heads-up — after merge 5150 we're seeing p99 generation latency spike in us-west-2 A10 canary pool during the canary window. Canary traffic ~5% and p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~1.1s. throughput looks steady though.

matt: saw it on the per-route dashboards, p50 unchanged. curious if this is CPU or IO. any node-level alerts?

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 5150 started (env: canary-usw2-A10) by matt at 2024-06-12T09:12:30Z

raj: grabbing perf traces and iostat/ps output from canary nodes now. starting with `iostat -x 1` to check device util.

raj: preliminary `iostat` shows /dev/nvme0n1 util at ~92% on a subset of nodes for sustained periods during the spike. Not all nodes, ~30% are hot.

ana: flamegraph and CPU stack sample from one noisy node — heavy in kernel selector and batch commit paths. Also seeing long tail in host->gpu memcpy stalls.

ana: flamegraph top breakdown (sample):
```
GPU scheduler                      32.1%
batcher::commit                    21.4%
kernel_selector::choose            18.7%
rt_io::nvme_submit                 12.5%
host_gpu_memcpy                    7.9%
other                              7.4%
```
\nkevin: quick note: PR 5150 changed the kernel selection heuristic and the fallback threshold. Previously we avoided fallback unless >4096 tokens; the change moves that to 2048 in some codepaths. That will increase fallback invocations and push more work into the IO/host path for many requests.

matt: that matches what we're seeing: more fallback => more host<->gpu memcpy + nvme interaction for KV prefix cache writes. Could explain high nvme util and memcpy stalls compounding latency.

lucy: we should stop the rollout and revert 5150 from canary until we understand. Can the rollout team revert?

jen: checked 5150 diff. It only touches runtime kernel selector heuristics and a small binder change. No DB migrations. Revert should be safe.

matt: prepping revert PR 5172 now. will land and promote revert to canary in ~10m unless objections.

raj: i will open a logging/metrics PR to emit `kernel_selector.fallback_count` and `node_nvme_util_percent` to make this visible per-node. Also we should track host_gpu_memcpy tail latencies.

ana: additional note from profiling — even on nodes where nvme util isn't saturated, fallback_count correlates with increased memcpy p99s. so fallback seems to hit a less-optimal execution path for many cases.

kevin: plan: add guard to avoid triggering fallback during periods of elevated nvme util and make the threshold adaptive. also add a unit/regression test that simulates nvme-saturated background IO. I'll open a follow-up PR after revert.

deploy-bot: Revert PR 5172 merged and canary promoted at 2024-06-12T09:39:10Z :white_check_mark:

lucy: monitoring canary now — p99 on canary nodes falling back to ~430ms within 3 minutes. keeping an eye on rollout. thanks everyone.

matt: follow-up action item: add CI perf scenario that injects background NVMe IO load to catch this class of regression earlier (ticket created: ENG-4523).

lucy: agreed. once rollout finishes and metrics are in, we'll re-evaluate a safer re-introduction with the adaptive guard. :thumbsup:
